text:
tessa: Hi all, first-day question. Just got an M1 Air and trying to standardize dev tools: asdf for node/python, Homebrew at /opt/homebrew, using fish as shell, and 1Password for SSH keys. Python builds fail with missing ssl/zlib. Also 1Password agent doesn't seem to expose keys to ssh. Any compact checklist or obvious gotchas?

rohan: welcome! quick checklist: 1) ensure Homebrew is the arm64 prefix (/opt/homebrew). 2) export brew paths before asdf/shims load. For fish: add to ~/.config/fish/config.fish:

set -x PATH /opt/homebrew/bin $PATH
set -x HOMEBREW_PREFIX /opt/homebrew

then restart fish.

mike: for python builds on mac/arm you typically need to point configure to openssl and zlib from brew. Example (bash/zsh envs shown, convert to fish with set -x):

export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib -L/opt/homebrew/opt/zlib/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include -I/opt/homebrew/opt/zlib/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib/pkgconfig:/opt/homebrew/opt/zlib/lib/pkgconfig"
asdf install python 3.11.4

that fixed it for me. If build still errors, paste the tail of the build log.

rohan: 1Password agent: two gotchas: a) the GUI agent and CLI can expose different sockets, b) if your session started before unlocking 1Password the env var won't be set. Check with:

lsof -U | rg 1password || gpgconf --list-dirs agent-ssh-socket
ssh-add -l

if ssh-add shows "The agent has no identities." re-export SSH_AUTH_SOCK to the socket path shown and re-run `ssh-add`.

mike: also, if you're migrating from pyenv/nvm, remove old shims in ~/.pyenv or /usr/local/bin to avoid which/python mismatch. Run `which python` and `asdf current`.

ops-bot: New hire reminder: complete the dev tooling checklist at https://intranet.redwood/dev-onboard and mark Step 2 when done.

dotfiles-bot: We have M1-specific notes at https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles/blob/main/macos/m1/SETUP.md. Please open a short PR if you add extra steps.

tessa: Thanks! I'll try the LDFLAGS/PKG_CONFIG_PATH trick and re-export SSH_AUTH_SOCK. I'll ping @mike if the logs still look weird. Appreciate the quick tips :pray:
